solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legendary king's son is terribly pushy

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of pushy are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mythical monarch's boy is described as dreadfully pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' is the anagram signal; the 's after king is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphus was the king of Corinth in Greek myth condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever.

clue.text: Misconstrued as spot of persuasive flattery

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly interpreted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little bit of coaxing praise gets misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misconstrued' rearranges AS SPOT OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-soap is smooth, wheedling flattery used to win someone over.

clue.text: Powerful Chinese nationalists rule out getting security devices

parts.note: strong means powerful

indicators.note: out means the next piece is removed

parts.note: the Boxers were the Chinese nationalists of the 1900 Boxer Rebellion

explanation.surface: Strong Chinese rebels end up obtaining safety equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rule out' removes R from BOXERS, leaving BOXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongboxes are lockable safes or chests used to keep valuables secure.

clue.text: Norm and I go through university together

parts.note: par is the norm or standard level
to pass is to go through, as with a law

explanation.surface: A man named Norm and the speaker go to university together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name but means average.
explanation.definitionFit: Pari passu is a Latin phrase meaning side by side, at an equal rate, simultaneously.

clue.text: Wear out of habit at college

parts.note: use means custom or habit, as in long use
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: Someone wears clothing out of habit while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something up is to exhaust or consume it completely.

clue.text: Most of the Irish coming around to a measure of frugality

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses its final letter
coming around turns the abbreviation for Irish back to front

parts.note: FT, a foot, is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Irish people are said to be warming to the idea of saving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of 'the'; 'coming around' turns the Irish abbreviation back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful, economical management of money, the same quality as frugality.

clue.text: Johnnie needs no introduction as a former PM

indicators.note: needs no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: johnnie is British slang for a condom, also called a sheath

explanation.surface: A man called Johnnie is so famous as an ex-prime minister he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnnie' looks like a name but is British slang for a condom; dropping its first letter leaves HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the British Conservative prime minister from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Disastrous to ignore daughter's anger

indicators.note: to ignore means the next piece is left out

parts.note: dire means dreadful or disastrous

explanation.surface: A daughter is furious at being ignored, which is disastrous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath or rage.

clue.text: House party held in ancient city at conclusion of fast

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter
held in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A feast held in an old city to mark the end of a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Injure German through a piece of armour by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the result is heard as another word

parts.words: German through a piece of armour
parts.note: G, the abbreviation for German, goes through A GREAVE, a greave being shin armour

explanation.surface: A German is wounded right through his armour.
explanation.walkthrough: G inside A GREAVE gives AGGREAVE; 'by the sound of it' turns that spelling into the word it is heard as.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to wrong or distress someone, causing them hurt.

clue.text: In favour of release without charge

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
to free someone is to release them

explanation.surface: Someone supports letting a prisoner go, with no charges brought.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given gratis costs nothing, so it comes without any charge.

clue.text: Enterprising leader of Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
a head is a leader, as of a school or department

explanation.surface: The chief minister of an Indian state is praised as dynamic.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives 'leader' first, but the answer puts the state first: GOA's HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is ambitious and keen to try new ventures, i.e. enterprising.

clue.text: Praised Pep's initial resolve to include new winger

indicators.note: to include means to take the next piece inside
to resolve something is to break it down and recombine it, so these letters are reordered
the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A football commentator praises Pep Guardiola's determination in signing a fresh wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' is the anagram signal and 'to include' the insertion. 'winger' looks like football but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper is a wading shore bird, and any bird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Remain undecided about joining Hearts

indicators.note: joining means the two pieces are set side by side

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
over means about, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Someone can't make up their mind about signing for Hearts football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which makes 'joining' read like a transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover over a decision is to waver, staying in a state of indecision.

clue.text: Colloquial dialect of unrefined Spaniard perhaps

parts.note: vulgar means coarse or unrefined
a Spaniard is an example of a Latin, a speaker of a Romance language

explanation.surface: A boorish Spaniard speaks in casual slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar Latin was the everyday spoken form of Latin from which the Romance languages grew.

clue.text: Fleischer film disregarding obstruction of Algerian nationalist leader

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving the next piece out

parts.note: Barabbas is a 1961 biblical epic directed by Richard Fleischer
a bar is an obstruction or barrier

explanation.surface: A film reference, minus a blockage, leads to a North African political figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding' removes BAR from the front of BARABBAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferhat Abbas led the Algerian independence movement and headed its provisional government.

clue.text: Weaken on account of earlier excessive use

indicators.note: earlier says the second piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: over means on account of, as in fighting over something
to kill a flavour or effect is to weaken or neutralise it

explanation.surface: Something was weakened because it had been overused before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' tells you the second idea goes first, even though the clue gives 'Weaken' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overkill is the use of far more force or effort than is needed.

clue.text: Dominated by Eve, Rob or Dicky

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was bossed around by one of two people, Eve or Rob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' rearranges EVE ROB OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear someone is to overpower them; the past tense means overpowered.

clue.text: Reduce the price of pink feathers

parts.note: an engine that pinks makes a knocking noise, so pink means knock
down is the soft fine feathers of a bird

explanation.surface: A shop marks down some pink plumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' looks like a colour but is the engine sense of knocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock down a price is to lower it, as in a sale.

clue.text: Row about Ms Halliwell's underwear

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a line is a row
Geri Halliwell is the former Spice Girl

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a pop star's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Former copper to consider accepting member's apology for slight impropriety

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: accepting means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: to see a matter is to consider it
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman considers a parliamentarian's apology for a minor lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. 'accepting' puts M inside SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite apology said after a burp, a bump, or interrupting.

clue.text: Somewhat womanish fellow from the Middle East

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A rather effeminate man from the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Disappear with earl's old hat

parts.note: to pass, as in pass away or pass out of sight, is to disappear

explanation.surface: A nobleman's antique hat goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' reads as a literal hat but is the idiom for outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of fashion, which is exactly what the French borrowing means.

clue.text: Record year covered by extremely pompous diarist

indicators.note: covered by means the pieces sit inside the next one
extremely points to the two end letters of the word

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A self-important diarist writes up his year.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of 'pompous' are P and S, wrapping EP and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept the famous diary of 1660s London life.

clue.text: Suppress some novel ideas

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stifles a few fresh ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit or suppress, as with a sound or passage left out.

clue.text: Spooner's US publicity agent to steal banner of anarchism

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: flack is American slang for a press agent or publicist
blag is British slang for to obtain by trickery or to rob

explanation.surface: An American PR man plans to steal an anarchist flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of FLACK and BLAG gives BLACK FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain black flag is the traditional emblem of anarchism.

clue.text: Colour of Balding's top mare is unusual

indicators.note: unusual suggests these letters are set out in an odd new order
the top of a down entry's word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Racehorse trainer Balding's best mare has a rare coat colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges B and MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a warm yellowish-orange shade, named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Girl stuffing mole into basket

indicators.note: stuffing means the first piece is packed inside the second

parts.note: a mole is a stone breakwater or jetty, much like a pier
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl crams a small burrowing animal into a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the animal but is a harbour wall; 'stuffing' puts the girl inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a basket, one of a pair slung across a horse, donkey or bicycle.

clue.text: Roll back a small piece

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: Someone sends back just a scrap of bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A nub is a small lump or stub, a little knob of something.

clue.text: Something to increase the effectiveness of electromagnets originally installed in flying robots

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside the next piece
flying suggests the letters of robots are thrown about into a new order
originally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A technical note about electromagnets fitted in airborne robots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges ROBOTS into BOOSTR; 'installed in' puts E inside before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A booster is anything that strengthens or amplifies, such as a vaccine dose or a rocket stage.

clue.text: Animals from leading breeders entered in auctions

indicators.note: entered in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: auctions are sales

indicators.note: leading points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Livestock from top breeders is put up at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sables are small furry mammals of the marten family prized for their pelts.

clue.text: Cannon formerly protecting road near the centre of Monaco

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round the next pieces

parts.note: once means formerly, as in once upon a time

indicators.note: near says the next piece sits right beside the first
the centre of a word means its middle letters

explanation.surface: Artillery that once guarded a road close to Monaco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' wraps the word for formerly round the road and the centre of Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military artillery, mounted guns such as cannon.
